goals.reason: One conceptual quantity: amount of specified elementary entities expressed in mol. Naming the entity and differentiating amount from mass are necessary interpretations of that quantity, not extra independent calculation routines. No new mass, gas-volume or general stoichiometric scope is added.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent current DE/EN. The mol symbol and specified entity must remain distinct from grammatical unit name or an unspecified bag of particles.
goals.memoryReason: A compact amount-of-substance/unit definition is a justified recall anchor. The preserved card explicitly ties mol to NA particles; selecting the counted entity and explaining the relation remain understanding performance.

goals.reason: One formula-composition and molar-mass translation into the mass/amount relation. Adding atomic contributions, respecting formula indices and interpreting g/mol belong to the same conversion. Mere unsupported substitution would be inadequate evidence; inverse and unequal-mass comparisons must preserve the shared amount basis.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent formula/atomic-mass basis and simple mass/amount scope; no experimental molar-mass determination or solution-concentration demand.
goals.memoryReason: The compact M=m/n relation is useful recall, with quantities explicitly named on the current card. The card does not establish formula-index understanding or dimensional justification.

goals.reason: One scale distinction between particle masses and macroscopic sample masses. Both u and g are mass units; u is not intrinsically a particle counter. Bridging particle mass to a sample via its particle count is part of this same scale interpretation, not a separate general conversion syllabus.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent units and limited particle/amount contexts. The familiar matching numerical values in u and g/mol are a school approximation, not an exact post2019 identity of units or quantities.
goals.memoryReason: The required performance is explaining scale, quantities and units from supplied particle-count data. An additional isolated numeric u-in-grams card is not necessary.

goals.reason: One proportional relation N=NA*n with named entity and unit mol^-1. Counting atoms inside molecules or formula units is an application of that specified-entity relation, not evidence that all mol samples contain equal numbers of atoms regardless of composition.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent interpretation and simple application of the proportionality factor. Modern exact/appropriately rounded NA must be distinguished from the retained historical HE constant.
goals.memoryReason: A stable Avogadro value/unit is a justified compact anchor. The existing approximation6.022e23 is appropriate; particle-type and proportional reasoning remain independent understanding.

goals.reason: One equal-volume/equal-particle-number explanation at equal temperature and pressure under the ideal-gas approximation. The model boundary and rejection of equal-mass inference are intrinsic to the stated law, not extra independent thermodynamics.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent gas-law scope. Equal conditions must include T and p; gas identity is not a guarantee of equal mass or equal real-gas behaviour near condensation.
goals.memoryReason: Contextual explanation of assumptions and counterexamples is primary. No extra fixed list or independent factual recall requirement is added.

goals.reason: One condition-bound conversion V=Vm*n. Interpreting V/n and why its value changes with conditions belongs to the same quantity. A universal22.4L/mol assertion would contradict the operative wording.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent specified-condition and simple volume/amount scope, without new ideal-gas-equation algebra or numerical constant recall requirement.
goals.memoryReason: The compact Vm=V/n relation is useful recall. The exact preserved card explicitly restricts the value to specified conditions; explanation of changed conditions remains understanding.

goals.reason: One inference of the molar mass of a gas, either from known formula composition or compatible mass/volume data. The two evidence routes estimate the same property; units, matched conditions and pure-gas/mixture limits belong to interpreting that inference.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent formula or simple gas-data route. Do not treat molar mass as changing with T/p or infer a unique compound identity from one molar-mass value.
goals.memoryReason: Existing M and Vm prerequisites supply compact relations. The new performance concerns combining and interpreting them, so no duplicated formula card is needed.

goals.reason: One particle-identity/notation competence for selected important elemental gases. Connecting the diatomic entity to indices and reaction coefficients is the same representation, not a separate full reaction-balancing syllabus. The title justify is interpreted through particle/evidence explanation, not an unintroduced orbital theory.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent selected-important-element scope. Neither language claims all elements or all gases are diatomic; molecular substances and monatomic noble gases must not be conflated.
goals.memoryReason: The operative competence requires explanation and correct model-based notation, not an exhaustive uncued gas list. Preserve the reviewed decision without inventing a new isolated list card.

goals.reason: One interpretation of qualitative elemental-analysis evidence through combustion products. Carbon and hydrogen channels jointly constrain the analyzed sample; controls and limits are necessary parts of this inference. It does not include quantitative mass percentages or empirical/molecular formula calculation.
goals.bilingual: Equivalent qualitative analysis and carbon/hydrogen interpretation. Positive CO2/water evidence alone cannot exclude additional elements or contamination; supplied test/blank observations remain data.
goals.memoryReason: The relevant achievement is contextual inference and control reasoning. No new rote reagent/colour card is necessary in this bounded package.

goals.reason: Accept the combined relative-mass/formula inference as one constrained model-evaluation competence using compatible experimental mass/volume/particle data and an explicit reference. The outcomes are coupled by composition and entity count; it is not a licence to add independent general mass-spectrometry, experimental design or structure-elucidation routines. Insufficient data must permit a nonunique conclusion.
goals.bilingual: DE/EN preserve both outcomes and gaseous-element/binary-compound scope. No scope is silently deleted merely to match the narrower BY9-other source.
goals.memoryReason: Fresh constrained inference, reference choices and model ambiguity are understanding performance. Prior symbolic vocabulary remains with prerequisites; another fixed answer/formula card would not establish it.

goals.reason: One formal conservation-based representation of a simple chemical reaction, including compatible partial/half equations and the overall equation. Using partial equations is not an independent redox mechanism/mastery claim. The DE second clause already exists and is supported separately by current BY10; it must not disappear from the EN description.
goals.bilingual: The proposed EN adds use half-equations and overall equations to describe chemical reactions, matching the existing DE. This does not demand previously absent independent complex-redox construction. General source uses of Teilgleichungen may also be non-redox partial equations; full source coverage is not asserted from this translation alone.
goals.prerequisiteLimit: Current symbol/reaction/mass-conservation chain is retained. Where an example uses electrons, charges or supplied half equations, their meaning must be provided unless independently secured; this review does not certify advanced ion/redox prerequisites from the present direct edges.
goals.memoryReason: Conservation, notation and cancellation need reasoning rather than recall of a fixed equation. The EN correction changes exact A/M fingerprints, so new truthful affected bindings are required despite unchanged DE content.

goals.reason: Charge-neutral ratio derivation/name translation and explaining physical salt properties are separately assessable demands. The narrower candidate preserves the formula competence but drops the existing property explanation. Current historical atomic status and fingerprint remain intact; their technical validity does not settle the substantive preservation issue.
goals.bilingual: Candidate DE/EN match one narrower formula competence, including supplied molecular-ion formula data. BY9-other explicitly limits its formula clause to binary salts; that narrower required scope cannot be silently promoted to a universal molecular-ion routine.
goals.sourceAndTargetLimit: Current950 is visible alongside965 in the author's recorded views, but generic simple structure-property relationships and a prerequisite edge do not prove full crystallinity/brittleness/conductivity preservation with actual source mappings and current D/P/A/M/V. Both BY salt clauses retain the property explanation.
goals.memoryReason: The old no_memory_needed record remains unmodified. No automatic new approval follows from either narrowing the goal or observing valid historical fingerprints.
